_comment: Claude Code Starter Pack - safety baseline. The safety net is three layers: the deny and ask rules below, two PreToolUse hooks (scripts/bash-safety-extended.py for secrets, edits to this safety layer, rm -rf, mv overwrites, download-and-run, disk writes, skipped git hooks and hidden deny-list commands; scripts/git-push-guard.py for direct pushes to main/master), and disableBypassPermissionsMode. The allow list covers day-to-day work (read-only inspection, build tools, media tooling, git, running your own scripts) so it does not nag; network tools that can send data out (curl, wget, ssh), package installs (pip, python -m pip, npm, brew, go install / go get, cargo install), code fetched and run on the spot (npx, go run pkg@version, docker run / docker pull), pushes and destructive commands stay in ask or deny. Ask outranks allow, so the ask rules carve installs out of broad allow rules such as python3 *, go *, cargo * and docker *. Precedence is deny, then ask, then allow, across every settings file: a project's .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json can add deny or ask rules, but an allow there cannot lift a deny or ask rule from this file. To loosen one, edit or remove it here.
_comment_hooks: The Read deny rules are the first line: they also cover Bash file commands such as cat and Grep (best effort), the credential stores the hook knows (kept in step with CREDENTIAL_LOCATIONS in scripts/bash-safety-extended.py by a test; Read(~/.claude*/.credentials.json) also covers Claude Code's login inside copies of ~/.claude such as the install backup ~/.claude.bak-<date>), and every .env / .env.* / .envrc under the working folder except .env.shared and templates (the ! carve-outs). The Read|Grep hook adds what the rules cannot express: env files anywhere on disk (including outside the working folder), symlinks resolved, and Grep content searches. The Bash|PowerShell|Monitor group also checks the Monitor tool's command like a Bash command; Claude Code offers that tool only when DISABLE_TELEMETRY below is removed. statusLine.refreshInterval re-runs the status line every 60 seconds so its reset countdowns and session time keep moving while the session is idle.
_comment_launcher: Every Python script runs through scripts/python-launcher.sh, so this one file works on macOS, Linux and Windows: it finds Python 3.9 or newer (python3, python, or the Windows py launcher, skipping the Microsoft Store placeholder and older versions) and caches the compiled scripts, which roughly halves the time each hook takes. 'guard' makes a safety hook block the call when no usable Python exists (Claude Code would otherwise let it through), 'quiet' leaves the status line empty instead. On Windows the hooks, the status line and the Bash tool run in Git Bash, which Git for Windows provides; it is required.
_comment_windows: Read rules use ~/ for the home folder on every system; on Windows Claude Code matches them against paths in /c/Users/<name>/... form, so ~/AppData/... covers C:\Users\<name>\AppData\.... CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=0 keeps Claude on the Bash tool: the safety hook reads bash commands, so a PowerShell tool next to it would be an unchecked way around it (with Git Bash installed, the Bash deny rules above already switch the PowerShell tool off; this makes it explicit). As a second lock, the safety hook's matcher also takes PowerShell and blocks every PowerShell tool call. To use the PowerShell tool anyway, accept that its commands go unchecked: set the variable to 1 and remove PowerShell from that matcher. On macOS and Linux the PowerShell tool is off unless enabled, so none of this changes anything there. Without Git Bash, Claude Code runs hooks through PowerShell, where `sh` does not exist: the hooks cannot start and Claude Code lets every call through, which is why Git for Windows is required.
_comment_teams: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS in env above unlocks the 'teammates' multi-agent feature (off by default in Claude Code). It only makes the capability available; summoning a team is always a deliberate, manual action, so it costs nothing on its own.
_comment_trust: The 'Do you trust the files in this folder?' dialog cannot be turned off from settings.json: no settings key or safe environment variable skips it, and bypass mode (which would) is deliberately locked off. Answer yes for this pack's clone and for folders you created or whose source you know: trusting a folder lets its own .claude/settings.json, hooks and .mcp.json servers run on your computer, outside these checks. Claude Code remembers the answer per folder.
_comment_cleanup: cleanupPeriodDays controls how many days Claude Code keeps local transcripts and other session data before deleting them; Claude Code's own default is 30. 3650 keeps them for 10 years, so /resume can return to past sessions for a long time. Transcripts hold everything Claude read, clients' personal data included: if you process client data, GDPR's storage-limitation principle argues for a shorter period, so set a lower number here. The minimum is 1; 0 fails validation.
